subject: maths
topic: Trigonometry: ratios, special angles, sine and cosine rules, bearings

kept.explanation: tan 45° = 1, cos 60° = 1/2, sin 90° = 1. So the expression becomes 1 + 2(1/2) - 1 = 1 + 1 - 1 = 1. These are standard special-angle values that must be memorised.

kept.q: Chidi walks from point X to point Y on a bearing of 070°. What is the bearing of X from Y (the back bearing)?
kept.explanation: The back bearing is found by adding 180° to the original bearing when it is less than 180°. So 070° + 180° = 250°. This gives the direction of X as seen from Y.
kept.pidgin: To find back bearing, if the first bearing less pass 180°, you go add 180° to am. So 070° + 180° = 250°. Na so you go take know where X dey if you dey stand for Y.

kept.q: From town Q, town P is located 6 km away on a bearing of 040°, while town R is located 10 km away on a bearing of 160°. Using the cosine rule, find the distance PR correct to the nearest kilometre.
kept.explanation: The angle PQR between the two bearings is 160° - 040° = 120°. By the cosine rule, PR^2 = QP^2 + QR^2 - 2(QP)(QR)cos(120°) = 36 + 100 - 2(6)(10)(-0.5) = 136 + 60 = 196. So PR = sqrt(196) = 14 km.
kept.pidgin: The angle between the two bearings na 160° - 040° = 120°. Cosine rule talk say PR^2 = 36 + 100 - 2(6)(10)cos(120°) = 136 + 60 = 196. So PR = sqrt(196) = 14 km.

q.q: In triangle ABC, angle A = 40°, angle B = 65°, and side a (opposite angle A) = 10 cm. Using the sine rule, find the length of side b (opposite angle B) to the nearest whole number.
q.explanation: By the sine rule, a/sin A = b/sin B, so b = (a × sin B)/sin A = (10 × sin 65°)/sin 40°. This gives b = (10 × 0.9063)/0.6428 ≈ 14.1, which rounds to 14 cm.
q.pidgin: Sine rule talk say a/sin A = b/sin B, so b = (10 × sin 65°)/sin 40°. Na (10 × 0.9063)/0.6428 ≈ 14.1, wey round to 14 cm.
